question: In a pedigree of an autosomal dominant trait it is observed that:

options.opa: The trait appears more frequently in males.
options.opb: The unaffected people do not transmit the trait.
options.opc: The trait tends to skip generations.
options.opd: The affected people have both affected parents.
options.ope: The trait tends to appear in the progeny of related parents.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Autosomal dominant trait" -> "trait appears in every generation" -> "unaffected people do not transmit the trait" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Autosomal dominant trait" -> "trait appears equally in males and females" -> "trait does not appear more frequently in males" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Autosomal dominant trait" -> "trait does not skip generations" -> "trait appears in every generation" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Autosomal dominant trait" -> "affected individuals can have one affected parent" -> "affected people do not need both affected parents" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Autosomal dominant trait" -> "trait appears regardless of parental relation" -> "trait does not specifically appear in progeny of related parents" -> 85%
analysis: In a pedigree of an autosomal dominant trait, the key characteristic is that the trait does not skip generations. Unaffected individuals do not carry the dominant allele and therefore do not transmit the trait to their offspring. This means that if an individual does not express the trait, they cannot pass it on. Therefore, the correct observation is that unaffected people do not transmit the trait.
